content.comment_body: Hello, I understand the fundamentals of programming [product_name], but I’m struggling to establish a simple connection between two [product_name] devices connected via a router. What is a straightforward method to, for example, trigger a light connected to the second [product_name] from a software output in the first? Alternatively, how should two network inputs/outputs be set up in the programming software? The [document] lacks detailed explanations, so I’m unclear about the proper configurations, such as TSAP and what to do if the trigger is from a function rather than an input. Could you clarify this for me? Thank you.

I’ve attached a video demonstrating how to connect two [product_name] devices and use switching commands between them. The video size required splitting into a two-part ZIP archive. You’ll need to download both files and extract the archive. The complete video is also included in my post from 10/12/2018 9:42 AM.

Here is the second part of the ZIP archive. For upload purposes, I had to rename the file. Once you've downloaded "2 [product_name] connected.z01.zip", please rename it to "2 [product_name] connected.z01". The full video is available in my post from 10/12/2018 at 9:42 AM.

Thank you, your video was clear and easy to follow. I successfully linked the two [product_name] devices. The solution was simply to connect the diagrams side by side in the software, which handles the process—very convenient!
Hello, I’m having trouble extracting the files. I can’t find "2 [product_name] connected.z01" and, even after renaming, the file remains as .zip.

Everything seems fine with the ZIP files; I just tested them. I’ll message the moderators to see if I can upload the full video to a file host. Then a moderator could download it and add it as an attachment.
Thank you—the video was very helpful.

I encountered the same issue but needed one extra step to make it work. The video’s steps are correct and everything works in the simulator, but for a physical device, I had to do the following: Go to File -> Properties -> General, then check 'Allow S7 Access' and 'Allow Modbus Access' (not sure if both are required, but enabling them made it work for me). Hope this helps others facing similar problems.
When I created the video, [product_name] version [version_no] did not exist yet. Devices before [product_name] [version_no] don’t have options to enable S7 or Modbus access.
